tasks.title: Lean Startup and MVP
tasks.titleZh: 精益创业与最小可行产品
tasks.transcript: When launching a new business, entrepreneurs face countless decisions, from choosing a target market to deciding which features to include in their first product. These choices can be overwhelming, especially when resources are limited and customer feedback is scarce. To address these challenges, some startups adopt a strategy that emphasizes speed, experimentation, and customer feedback. This approach, known as the Lean Startup methodology, was popularized by Eric Ries and has gained traction in the tech world and beyond. One of its core practices is building a Minimum Viable Product, or MVP. This is a basic version of a new product released quickly to gather feedback from early users. The goal is to learn what works and what doesn't, so that future development is guided by actual user experience rather than assumptions. Another key idea is validated learning: teams test their ideas by putting the product out in the real world. This helps them figure out whether their product actually meets the needs of their customers. In all fairness, I should point out that this approach isn't perfect. Rapid iteration and constant change can sometimes lead to confusion or a lack of clear direction, and in the pursuit of efficiency, some teams may cut corners which could affect product quality. Still, many entrepreneurs find the lean startup methodology helpful for navigating the uncertainties of launching a new product.
